subject: URGENT: HarborTech AZ2 throughput collapse — request for regional evacuation authorization
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@harbortech.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:12:04 -0700
Subject: Realtime: spike in 5xx + severe latency in us-west-az2

Hey Lauren —

We just saw a sharp jump in request latencies and 5xx rates for our HarborTech production traffic routed to us-west-az2 starting ~08:45PT. User-facing timeouts and retries are spiking; our telemetry shows queues backing up on inference nodes. This is impacting checkout flows; we're getting multiple customer complaints.

Can Redwood initiate an emergency re-route to us-west-az1 and us-east-1? We need an immediate mitigation and ETA for stabilization. Attaching a screenshot of the dashboard.

— Alex
HarborTech, Sr. SRE
Attachments: harbortech_metrics_0900.png (image)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@harbortech.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 5xx + severe latency in us-west-az2

Alex — thanks for the ping and the graph. We're treating this as P0.

Immediate steps we can take now:
- Initiate cross-AZ evacuation: drain us-west-az2 for production traffic and shift steady-state to us-west-az1 + us-east-1.
- Enable degraded routing profile for HarborTech (lower concurrency, prefer lower-latency variants).
- Open a customer bridge — I'll join now.

Rishi — please confirm impact to SLA and whether we need exec approval for cross-region failover (possible mitigation may have billing/route-commit implications).

Marissa & Hannah — I'll need comms for HarborTech and the exec note if we escalate. Alex, can you confirm if HarborTech will accept brief degraded throughput and increased p99 during the failover window?

— Lauren
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:25:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 5xx + severe latency in us-west-az2

Lauren — I recommend we proceed with evacuation immediately. Notes:
- SLA impact: temporary p99 increases expected; no SLA credit triggers unless errors >1% for 30m. Current 5xx is ~2% and rising — keep monitoring.
- Authorization: For customers on our standard terms, routing changes within region are covered; cross-region (to eastus) is allowed under emergency routing — but we should log an exec exception to cover any overprovisioning costs if HarborTech wants guaranteed throughput.
- I'll approve an emergency cross-region drain for P0 mitigation. Please record in the incident ticket. 

Rishi
Head of Reliability
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@harbortech.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:33:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 5xx + severe latency in us-west-az2

Alex — thank you. We're initiating the evacuation and will update the bridge URL in 5 minutes. Expect a short period of increased p50/p90 while caches repopulate.

Actions taken:
- Routed 60% of new traffic off us-west-az2 within 3 minutes.
- Draining remaining workers with graceful handoff; KV cache warmup in progress.
- Degraded routing profile applied for HarborTech.

Alex — please confirm degraded-throughput tolerance. If you need full capacity, we can also open a temporary burst pool in us-east-1 (requires authorization for cost uplift).

— Lauren
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@harbortech.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 13:47:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 5xx + severe latency in us-west-az2

Lauren — confirmed. HarborTech accepts degraded throughput for the next 90 minutes. Appreciate the fast action and the transparent updates. Please send the incident summary and any cost implications; we'll loop in procurement if needed.

— Alex
